'''James William White IV''' (born October 21, 1982) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and current player development coach for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].{{cite web |url= https://www.si.com/college/cincinnati/news/former-uc-basketball-star-james-white-joins-minnesota-timberwolves-coaching-staff |title= Former UC Basketball Star James White Joins Minnesota Timberwolves Coaching Staff |last=Heltman |first=Russ |date=August 3, 2023 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] si.com|access-date=August 3, 2023 |language=English |trans-title= Former UC Basketball Star James White Joins Minnesota Timberwolves Coaching Staff}} White is well known for his athleticism and ability to dunk. Since high school, his most famous dunk has been the between-the-legs dunk, with many variations. He is also known for his ability to jump from the free throw line and dunk a basketball with both hands. 'Flight' White was a runner-up in two notable dunk contests: behind future [[University of Florida]] and [[Golden State Warriors]] power forward [[David Lee (basketball)|David Lee]] in the 2001 [[McDonald's]] High School Slam Dunk Contest, and behind North Carolina's [[David Noel]] in the NCAA College Slam Dunk Contest during the 2006 Final Four weekend. ==College career== White played his freshman year at the [[University of Florida]] in the 2001–02 season helping the Gators to a 22–9 record. He saw action in all but two games, making a pair of starts and averaged 20.5 minutes of playing time. He posted averages of 6.1 points and 2.9 rebounds. He transferred to the [[University of Cincinnati]], and after sitting out in the 2002–03 season, he became a starter for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats#Men's basketball|Bearcats]] in his three years with them, including his senior year when he averaged 16.3 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2 assists, 1.2 steals, and 0.9 blocks. ===2003–04 season=== White made his Cincinnati debut in mid-December 2003 vs. [[Middle Tennessee]], playing for the first time since March 2002,{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=233542132 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519201712/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=233542132 |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 19, 2017 |title=(16) CINCINNATI 89, MIDDLE TENN ST 54 – Recap |publisher=ESPN |date=December 20, 2003 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} scoring eight points in 19 minutes of action.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=233542132 |title=Middle Tennessee State 54, (12) Cincinnati 89 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=December 20, 2003 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} Tallied 14 points in the win over Miami (December 27, 2003),{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=233612132 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519201500/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=233612132 |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 19, 2017 |title=Cincinnati continues its unbeaten run |publisher=ESPN |date=December 27, 2003 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} while also dishing out four assists. Moved into the starting lineup vs. [[DePaul University|DePaul]] (January 11, 2004), replacing injured Armein Kirkland, and became a fixture. Tallied 12 points, five rebounds and three assists vs. [[University of Louisville|Louisville]] (January 21, 2004).{{cite web|author=Freedom Hall, Louisville, KY |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=240210097 |title=(12) Cincinnati 66, Louisville 93 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=January 21, 2004 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} He had 12 points and four rebounds at [[Wake Forest University|Wake Forest]] (February 15, 2004).{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=240460154 |title=(12) Cincinnati 85, (16) Wake Forest 91 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=February 15, 2004 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} He lettered in the spring for the C-USA champion UC track and field team. Qualified for NCAA Regionals in the [[high jump]] and [[triple jump]]. Named C-USA co-Player of the Week after averaging 14.5 points, 8.0 assists and 7.0 rebounds while shooting 69 percent from the field in a pair of UC wins (February 23–29). Scored 23 points and grabbed 11 rebounds, both then-career highs, in the win over [[Saint Louis University (United States)|Saint Louis]] (February 25, 2004),{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=240562132 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519221851/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=240562132 |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 19, 2017 |title=White: Career-high 23 points, 11 rebounds |publisher=ESPN |date=February 25, 2004 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} also recording seven assists, three steals and two blocked shots.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=240562132 |title=Saint Louis 52, (12) Cincinnati 77 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=February 25, 2004 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} He dished out nine assists at Charlotte (February 28, 2004).{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=240592429 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160805151818/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=240592429 |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 5, 2016 |title=(12) Cincinnati 75, Charlotte 67 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=February 28, 2004 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} He scored nine points, grabbed eight rebounds and had six assists in the C-USA semifinal win over Saint Louis (March 12, 2004).{{cite web|author=U.S. Bank Arena, Cincinnati, OH |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=240722132 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519221934/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=240722132 |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 19, 2017 |title=Saint Louis 46, (12) Cincinnati 66 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=March 12, 2004 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} He started the final 21 games of the season and took on a larger share of the ball-handling responsibilities in the final eight contests. He became team assists leader (3.6) who averaged 4.8 assists over the final eight games. He dished out seven assists and gathered six rebounds in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] opening round win over [[East Tennessee State University|East Tennessee State]] (March 19, 2004).{{cite web|author=Nationwide Arena, Columbus, OH |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=244000020 |title=(13) East Tennessee State 77, (4) finished with 11 points and tied a career high with 11 rebounds. He tallied 15 points and had six rebounds in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] opening round win over Iowa on March 17, 2005.{{cite web|author=RCA Dome, Indianapolis, IN |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=254000042 |title=(10) Iowa 64, (7) Cincinnati 76 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=March 17, 2005 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} He became team leader in assists (3.1) and scored in double digits 19 times. ===2005–06 season=== White scored 21 points in a win over Murray State (November 19, 2005),{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=253232132 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231022042954/https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=253232132 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 22, 2023 |title=Cincinnati 79, Murray State 75 (OT) – Recap |publisher=ESPN |date=November 19, 2005 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} making a steal and dunk in the final seconds of regulation to send the game into overtime. He scored 18 points on 7-of-9 shooting and had seven rebounds, and three steals in the win over [[Vanderbilt University|Vanderbilt]] (December 10, 2005),{{cite web|author=Memorial Gym, Nashville, TN |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=253440238 |title=Cincinnati 92, Vanderbilt 83 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=December 10, 2005 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} sinking a career-high four treys. Rallied UC from a five-point deficit in the final two and a half minutes of the win over [[Louisiana State University|LSU]] (December 23, 2005),{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=253572132 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519201557/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=253572132 |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 19, 2017 |title=Cincinnati 75, LSU 72 – Recap |publisher=ESPN |date=December 23, 2005 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} hitting back-to-back 3-pointers at the 2:27 and 1:51 marks and a pair of clinching free throws at 0:17. Tallied a season-high 23 points vs. [[North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University|North Carolina A&T]] (December 30, 2005),{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=253642132 |title=North Carolina A&T 69, Cincinnati 105 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=December 30, 2005 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} matching personal bests with four 3-point field goals and four steals. He tallied 22 points, making 4-of-6 treys, and hit a 3-pointer to put UC in the lead with 2:57 to play in the win over Providence (February 17, 2006), and also grabbing seven rebounds.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=260482132 |title=Providence 64, Cincinnati 66 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=February 17, 2006 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} He scored 17 points, going 3-of-5 from 3-point range, and had four assists vs. Seton Hall (February 28, 2006).{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=260592550 |title=Cincinnati 62, Seton Hall 72 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=February 28, 2006 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} White scored a career-high 32 points, including a career-high five three-pointers, in a narrow loss to [[Syracuse Orange|Syracuse]] on March 8.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=260672132 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170518102146/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=260672132 |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 18, 2017 |title=Syracuse beats buzzer, keeps NCAA hopes alive |publisher=ESPN |date=March 8, 2006 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} He became team scoring leader (15.9) who has reached double figures in all but four games. Topped the 1,000-point mark in career scoring with 1,209 points, 1,027 scored during his three seasons as a Bearcat to become the 44th member of UC's 1,000-point club. Leads the team in free throw percentage (.839) and is second in steals (1.1), assists (2.1), blocks (0.8) and third in rebounding (5.0). Named to the Las Vegas Holiday Classic all-tournament team after averaging 18.8 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 1.8 steals in the four wins. ==Professional career== ===NBA=== He was selected in the second round (31st overall) by the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in the [[2006 NBA draft]],{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/whiteja02.html|title= James White |publisher= Basketball-Reference.Com |access-date= November 15, 2012}} and his rights were immediately traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] for the rights to the Pacers' pick at No. 45 overall ([[Alexander Johnson (basketball)|Alexander Johnson]]), and second-round draft choices in [[2007 NBA Draft|2007]] and [[2008 NBA Draft|2008]]. In eight preseason games with Indiana, White averaged 3.8 points and 2.0 rebounds in 17.5 minutes a game over 8 preseason games. He was cut by the Indiana Pacers on October 31, 2006, with coach [[Rick Carlisle]] saying his release was the most difficult cut he has been involved with in his coaching career. White signed a two-year contract with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] on November 3, 2006.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/white_061103.html |title=Spurs Sign James White |publisher=NBA |access-date=December 2, 2011}} On December 16, 2006, the Spurs assigned White to play in their [[NBA Development League]] affiliated team the [[Austin Toros]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/white_assigned_061216.html |title=Spurs Assign James White to Austin |publisher=NBA |access-date=December 2, 2011}} He was recalled on December 26, but reassigned to Austin three days later.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_06-07.html |title=NBA Development League: 2006–07 D-League Transactions |publisher=NBA |access-date=December 2, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150618011602/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/transactions_06-07.html |archive-date=June 18, 2015 }} Spurs coach [[Gregg Popovich]] stated that the reason for the move was that the in-season schedule does not allow much time to practice and the veteran-heavy team does not allow any spare minutes for White. He continued to receive his salary from the Spurs while playing for the Toros. Toros coach [[Dennis Johnson]] stated that White received regular playing time.[http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/basketball/nba/spurs/stories/MYSA121706.11C.BKNspurs.notebook.36e0fd8.html Spurs notebook: White heading to NBDL team] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070113014246/http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/basketball/nba/spurs/stories/MYSA121706.11C.BKNspurs.notebook.36e0fd8.html |date=January 13, 2007 }} After playing in 15 games (with 11 starts), and averaging 16.3 points, 4.0 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 1.67 steals in 34.4 minutes, White was recalled by the Spurs for the second time on January 27, 2007.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/james_white_070127.html |title=Spurs Recall James White From Toros |publisher=NBA |access-date=December 2, 2011}} He had hitherto not seen any playing time with the Spurs. On March 26, White made his NBA debut with the Spurs against the [[Golden State Warriors]], scoring 9 points and grabbing 3 rebounds in 14 minutes during his first game.{{cite web|author=ORACLE Arena, Oakland, CA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=270326009 |title=Spurs 126, Warriors 89 – Box score |publisher=ESPN |date=March 26, 2007 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} White also got the first NBA start of his career on April 16, 2007, in a loss against the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. In a game where the Spurs rested their regular lineup due to the playoff standings already having been decided, White responded by scoring a career-high 17 points in 39 minutes of play in a 101–91 loss to the Grizzlies.{{cite web|author=FedExForum, Memphis, TN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270416029 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220082807/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270416029 |url-status=dead |archive-date=December 20, 2016 |title=Spurs rest regulars, lose to Grizzlies |publisher=ESPN |date=April 16, 2007 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} He averaged 8.2 PPG in 6 games for the Spurs. He was waived during the off-season by the Spurs on July 23, 2007[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/white_070723.html Spurs Waive James White], ''nba.com'', posted July 23, 2007 and received an NBA championship ring.[http://blogs.hoopshype.com/blogs/white/2007/11/17/5/ Turkish Adventure] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111003130011/http://blogs.hoopshype.com/blogs/white/2007/11/17/5/ |date=October 3, 2011 }}, ''hoopshype.com'', posted November 17, 2007 ===Europe=== On September 8, 2007, White joined [[Will Solomon]] when he signed a four-year contract with the [[Turkish Basketball League]] club [[Fenerbahçe Ülker|Fenerbahçe]]{{cite web |url=http://www.fenerbahce.org/eng/detay.asp?ContentID=1278 |title=James White joins Fenerbahce |publisher=Fenerbahce.org |date=October 8, 2007 |access-date=December 2, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071012003718/http://fenerbahce.org/eng/detay.asp?ContentID=1278 |archive-date=October 12, 2007}} who played in the [[Euroleague 2007-08|2007–08]] [[Euroleague 2007-08#Quarterfinals 2|Euroleague quarter finals]]. On March 22, 2008, White won the Turkish dunk contest against Curtis Withers, [[Quinton Hosley]], and Richard Chaney in the [[Turkish Basketball League|Beko Allstar Slam Dunk Contest]] with his raceway dunk.{{cite web|url=http://fanatik.ekolay.net/Fanatik/Default.aspx?aType=Detail&articleID=103577&catid=28 |title=White the Flight |access-date=December 2, 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080523065121/http://fanatik.ekolay.net/Fanatik/Default.aspx?aType=Detail&Catid=28&articleid=103577 |archive-date=May 23, 2008 }} ===Return to the NBA=== He was playing with the [[Anaheim Arsenal]] in the NBA's [[D-League]] when he signed a 10-day contract with the Houston Rockets on March 3, 2009, and then a second 10-day contract before signing a multi-year deal with the Rockets on March 24, 2009.[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4011883 Rockets Sign White] ESPN, March 24, 2009 He was deactivated April 7 to make room for forward [[Carl Landry]], who had recovered from a gunshot wound.{{cite web|author=BRIAN McTAGGART, Copyright 2009 Houston Chronicle |url=http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/6363509.html |title=Rockets activate Landry for Magic game – Houston Chronicle |work=Houston Chronicle |date=April 7, 2009 |access-date=December 2, 2011}} On September 2, 2009, White was drafted in the first round of the NBA Development League expansion draft by the [[Maine Red Claws]]. In September 2009, the Rockets traded White to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for the draft rights to [[Axel Hervelle]].[http://www.seattlepi.com/scorecard/nbanews.asp?articleID=264957 Nuggets acquire White]{{Dead link|date=February 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}. Retrieved on September 23, 2009. His first game with the Nuggets was on October 1, 2009, facing Utah. He scored 13 points, 10 of them from free throws.{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba/boxscore?gid=2009100126 |title=Utah 103, Denver 87 – Box score |publisher=Sports.yahoo.com |access-date=December 2, 2011 |archive-date=October 23, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023004524/http://sports.yahoo.com/nba/boxscore?gid=2009100126 |url-status=dead }} He was waived by the Nuggets on October 21, 2009.[http://realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/62258/20091021/denver_waives_james_white/ Denver Waives James White] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091024030737/http://www.realgm.com/src_wiretap_archives/62258/20091021/denver_waives_james_white/ |date=October 24, 2009 }}. ===Return to Europe=== He signed a contract with [[Spartak St. Petersburg]] of the [[Russian Basketball Super League|Russian Super League]] on November 10, 2009.[http://www.bc-spartak.ru/news/294 Джеймс Уайт – новый игрок "Спартака"] {{in lang|ru}} In 2010, he joined the Italian team [[Dinamo Sassari]] in [[Lega Basket Serie A]] where he was the 2010–11 Italian League top scorer, averaging 20.2 points in 34 games. In August 2011, he signed a one-year contract with [[Victoria Libertas Pesaro|Scavolini Pesaro]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/serie-a/30206/scavolini_siviglia_pesaro_announces_james_white.html |title=Scavolini Siviglia Pesaro announces James White |publisher=Sportando.net |access-date=December 2, 2011}} ===Second return to NBA=== [[File:James White.jpg|thumb|right|White with the [[New York Knicks]] in 2013]] On July 11, 2012, White signed a two-year deal with the [[New York Knicks]] for the veteran's minimum.{{cite web | title=Knicks Sign Free Agent G James White | website=CBS News - New York | date=2012-07-11 | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/knicks-sign-free-agent-g-james-white/ | access-date=2024-12-21}} White played with the New York Knicks' Summer League Team in Las Vegas, Nevada, in the summer of 2012. White averaged 6.3 points per game, 4.3 [[rebounds per game]], and 3.3 [[assists per game]].{{cite web|title=James White Summer League 2012 Statistics|url=http://www.nba.com/summer-league/2012/players/sl_james_white/|work=NBA.com|access-date= July 30, 2012}} On December 18, 2012, he was assigned to the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] of the [[NBA D-League]].[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/new_york_knicks_assign_chris_c_2012_12_18.html New York Knicks Assign Chris Copeland and James White to NBA D-League Affiliate Erie BayHawks] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150320090343/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/new_york_knicks_assign_chris_c_2012_12_18.html |date=March 20, 2015 }} He was recalled on December 19, reassigned on December 20,[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/knicks_assign_copeland_white_2012_12_20.html New York Knicks Re-Assign Chris Copeland and James White to NBA D-League Affiliate Erie BayHawks] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203042547/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/knicks_assign_copeland_white_2012_12_20.html |date=December 3, 2013 }} and recalled again on December 21.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/knicks_recall_three_from_bayha_2012_12_21.html Knicks Recall Three from BayHawks] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150210180106/http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/knicks_recall_three_from_bayha_2012_12_21.html |date=February 10, 2015 }} On February 7, 2013, it was announced that White would represent the Knicks in the slam dunk contest at the [[2013 NBA All-Star Game]] in Houston. He also scored a career high 20 points that year. On June 30, 2013, White was waived by the Knicks.[http://knicksnow.com/posts/3644/knicks-waive-james-white Knicks Waive James White] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130703062957/http://knicksnow.com/posts/3644/knicks-waive-james-white |date=July 3, 2013 }} ===Return to Europe=== On September 19, 2013, he returned to Italy and signed a one-year deal with [[Pallacanestro Reggiana|Grissin Bon Reggio Emilia]].{{cite news|title=Pallacanestro Reggiana announced James White|url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/serie-a/63592/pallacanestro-reggiana-announced-james-white.html|access-date=September 19, 2013|newspaper=Sportando.net}} During the season with Grissin Bon Reggio Emilia he averaged 17.1 points and 5 rebounds in 34 Italian League games and also helped his team to win the EuroChallenge title. On August 7, 2014, he signed a one-year deal with [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]] of Russia.{{cite news|title=Unics Kazan signs high flier White|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/140052/180|access-date=August 7, 2014|work=Euroleague.net|date=August 7, 2014}} On July 30, 2015, he signed with [[KK Cedevita|Cedevita Zagreb]] of Croatia for the 2015–16 season.{{cite news|title=Cedevita agreed with James White |url=http://www.abaliga.com/a9975/News/Cedevita_agreed_with_James_White.html |access-date=July 30, 2015 |work=Abaliga.com |date=July 30, 2015 |url-status=unfit |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150802003732/http://www.abaliga.com/a9975/News/Cedevita_agreed_with_James_White.html |archive-date=August 2, 2015 }} ===Iran=== In August 2016, White signed with [[Petrochimi Bandar Imam BC|Petrochimi Bandar Imam]] of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League]].[http://www.eurobasket.com/Croatia/news/460899/Petrochimi-tabs-James-White Petrochimi tabs James White] ===BIG3=== In the [[2017 Big3 season|summer of 2017]], James White joined [[Trilogy (basketball)|Trilogy]] of the [[BIG3]] league together with [[Al Harrington]], [[Rashad McCants]], and [[Kenyon Martin]]. Trilogy went undefeated throughout the inaugural season and won the first ever BIG3 championship. White also won the defensive player of the year award.{{Cite web |date=August 23, 2017 |title=BIG3 2017 Player Awards |url=https://big3.com/news/big3-2017-player-awards/ |access-date=May 29, 2022 |website=BIG3 |language=en-US}} White was a member of Trilogy when they won the [[2021 Big3 season|2021 BIG3 Championship]],{{Cite web |date=September 4, 2021 |title=TRILOGY WINS CHAMPIONSHIP! |url=https://big3.com/news/2021-big3-championship-recap/ |access-date=May 29, 2022 |website=BIG3 |language=en-US}} making him the first two-time BIG 3 Champion either as a player or coach.{{Cite web
